basics.name: Rajesh Shrestha
basics.label: Computer Science Ph.D. Researcher
basics.summary: Computer Science Ph.D. researcher at Oregon State University, advised by Prof. Xiao Fu, with expected graduation in December 2026. Research interests include generative AI, diffusion and flow models, multimodal and representation learning, computer vision, numerical optimization, scalable machine learning, and inverse problems. Approximately three years of industry ML engineering experience at Fusemachines.

work.name: Oregon State University
work.summary: Generative modeling, optimization-based inference, and interactive learning.
highlights: Developed a convergent plug-and-play framework integrating score-based denoisers into ADMM (first-author ICLR 2026 paper).
Design conditioning and sampling algorithms that adapt pretrained diffusion models to inverse problems without task-specific retraining.
Study synchronization in diffusion and flow models for correlated generations and shared structure.
Develop scalable ADMM algorithms and recoverability guarantees for compressed and quantized measurements.
Collaborate with OSU Physics on single-pixel spectral reconstruction using diffusion and representation-learning priors.
Developed interactive learning methods for noisy and evolving human feedback with Prof. Arash Termehchy.

work.name: Oregon State University
highlights: Designed programming assignments and automated grading infrastructure; supported students through technical discussions and individualized guidance.

work.name: Fusemachines Inc.
work.summary: Promoted from Associate to Level 2 and Level 3 Machine Learning Engineer.
highlights: Developed and deployed advertising recommendation models and evaluated changes through A/B testing, counterfactual analysis, and hypothesis testing.
Built ETL, training, and model-refresh pipelines with Apache Spark, Jenkins, AWS Lambda, and Amazon Redshift, supporting millions of push notifications per day.
Contributed to production document AI using image registration, OCR, clustering, and CRNN-based text recognition.
Contributed to Nepali speech recognition using recurrent neural networks, CTC loss, and EESEN.
Supervised and mentored two ML engineers and supported technical recruiting and project planning.

work.name: Robotics Club, Pulchowk Campus
work.position: Team Member, ABU Robocon International Robotics Competition
work.summary: Represented Nepal in ABU Robocon and contributed to award-winning autonomous robotic systems.
highlights: Implemented kinematics and control algorithms for differential-drive, omni-drive, and Stewart-platform robots and designed robot control circuits.

volunteer.summary: Volunteered in the earthquake relief program in Nepal. My work involved distributing relief materials including food, blankets and tents to the affected people. I also worked in the installation of temporary shelters and toilets along with data collection regarding the damage caused by the earthquake.
